title: Subsequences and polynomial-variable regularity
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $f_1,\dots,f_r$ elements which do not generate the unit ideal. Every order-preserving subsequence is regular iff the elements $f_iX_i$ form a regular sequence in the multivariate polynomial ring.

source.place: the coefficientwise ideal computation in Stacks Algebra Tag 07DW

proof.text: Identify the ideal generated by the first i terms of List.ofFn (C(f_j) X_j) with the span of the corresponding Fin i range. Apply the membership half of [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ideal-coefficients-monomial]: p lies in this prefix ideal precisely when coeff_E(p) lies in I_E = (f_j : j < i and E_j != 0). A term i : Fin r implies r >= 1, so the coefficient theorem applies even though the final equivalence permits r = 0.

For fixed i, the ideals I_E and I_(E+epsilon_i) coincide, since every generating index j is smaller than i. Multiplication by C(f_i) X_i is injective modulo the prefix ideal iff f_i a in I_E implies a in I_E for every E and a. In the forward direction test the polynomial a X^E, whose product is the single monomial f_i a X^(E+epsilon_i). In the reverse direction read the coefficient at E+epsilon_i of the product and apply the coefficient membership criterion to every E. Translate ideal cancellation into IsSMulRegular on the quotient using Mathlib isSMulRegular_quotient_iff_mem_of_smul_mem.

Assume every subsequence is regular. Given i and E, filter the increasing list of all indices by j < i and E_j != 0, and append i. The resulting increasing list maps under f to a sublist of List.ofFn f. Its last regular_mod_prev condition gives f_i a in I_E implies a in I_E. Apply the preceding one-step criterion for every i to obtain weak polynomial regularity.

Conversely assume polynomial weak regularity, hence the one-step coefficient cancellation conditions. Represent any sublist as f mapped over a sublist s of the increasing finite index list. At position k take i = s[k] and E = sum_(j in (s.take k).toFinset) epsilon_j. Its support is exactly the preceding selected indices, all less than i. Therefore I_E is the ideal generated by the preceding terms of this subsequence. The cancellation criterion supplies regular_mod_prev at every position. This argument tracks indices rather than distinct values, so it permits repeated f_j.

The given proper ideal makes R nontrivial. Each subsequence ideal is contained in the full family ideal, hence proper. The ideal of all C(f_i) X_i is contained in the kernel of constantCoeff, so it cannot contain 1 over the nontrivial ring R. These properness conditions upgrade both weak regularity statements to IsRegular. With r = 0 the injectivity conditions are vacuous and the same properness arguments prove the empty-sequence case.
